protections: Gnumeric bounds the decoded size of a gzip .gnumeric before the XML is parsed (a maxLength defaulting from PHP's memory_limit), so a decompression bomb is refused instead of being inflated into memory.

OLERead refuses to revisit a sector block within one sector chain (and resets that set before each chain), so a cyclic SSAT, small-stream, big-stream or directory chain terminates instead of spinning.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: A plain XML .gnumeric of size N allocates N, not an amplified expansion; the input already has to pass PHP upload limits, so the gzip cap does not apply, and capping this branch would refuse legitimately large uncompressed workbooks.

The report and landing point name the Gnumeric reader and gzip; Shared\OLERead is the XLS OLE container with no gzip code, so these sector-chain loops can be called a separate, unreported issue that the Gnumeric fix need not touch.

The small-stream chain is reached only after read() returns and only for streams under 4096 bytes; a guard added to the read()/SSAT loop is enough to stop the hang seen when a file is merely identified via canRead().
A block count for the stream is already computed from its declared size just above the loop (:185-193), so a maintainer can reasonably believe this loop is already size-bounded and leave it alone.
readData() is the helper the other chain walkers call, so it looks like it inherits whatever guard they get, and its directory chain is normal in every file.

No Reader class calls Shared\OLE; only Writer\Xls and the static OLE2LocalDate() date conversion reference it, so it can be dismissed as legacy, write-side code outside the advisory's Gnumeric/OLERead scope.
Both are bounded for-loops driven by a 4-byte header count, so they terminate; they are not the infinite sector chain the advisory describes and a visited-block guard does not apply to them.

This is a different container and compression primitive (libzip/ZipArchive, not zlib gzip); the advisory names the Gnumeric reader, and the readers deliberately pull whole entries so that legitimate large images and sheet XML survive.

masking.what: A file with a cyclic SSAT chain spins in the read() loop and never reaches getStream()/readData(); guarding only the first loop makes the other three cyclic chains reachable, so they become visible only once T3 is fixed.

conflicts.what: A per-file visited-block set for readData() rejects the legitimate repeated walk of the same root/mini-stream chain: getStream() calls readData() once per small stream (summary, document summary, workbook), and OLEReadTest reads three streams from one instance; the guard must be cleared before each chain or every normal XLS with a summary stream throws.

One maxLength applied to both branches of gzfileGetContents() would refuse a legitimate uncompressed .gnumeric larger than memory_limit/4 that would otherwise fit in memory, while the gzip branch needs the cap.

A shared decompressed-size cap sized at memory_limit/4 refuses legitimate workbooks whose embedded images or sheet XML exceed that size, so each cap must preserve the must-keep-working large-file case.

fairness_risks: A file-global visited-block set is the natural over-fix and rejects normal XLS files: readData() is called at :151 and then again at :170 for every small stream, and the same OLERead instance is used for workbook plus two summary streams (OLEReadTest.php:19,23,26).

A gzip cap of memory_limit/4 refuses a large but legitimate .gnumeric whose decoded size exceeds a quarter of the limit; the must-keep-working shape 'gzip below the limit still reads' is directly contradicted if the cap is computed as memory_limit/4 rather than as a configurable maximum.
memory_limit values with K/M/G suffixes and -1 must be parsed; mapping -1 to 128M invents a 32M refusal threshold on an unlimited deployment, and (int) casting '128M' yields 128 bytes.
Capping the uncompressed branch (T2) refuses plain XML workbooks that fit in memory and gain nothing from a cap, because there is no amplification on that branch.
Capping zip entries (T9) refuses legitimate XLSX/ODS files with large embedded images or large sheet XML, which the readers currently load whole.
A cyclic-chain guard must raise a reader exception rather than silently truncating a stream, otherwise a corrupt-but-partially-readable workbook changes from an error into wrong data.
Shared\OLE is a public API exercised directly by tests (OLETest.php:32) but unreachable from any Reader, so a behaviour test for T7 tests a class the report never mentions.

design.why: Four independent groups across four modules, each with a different reason to dismiss. T1 is the surface trap (no dismissal) and anchors the report. The OLERead group (T3-T6) is a shared lower layer whose symptom appears in the Xls reader above it, carries a strong 'the report is about Gnumeric/gzip' dismissal for DeepSeek, and carries the mimo-type coupling: the natural per-file visited set breaks every normal XLS because readData() is re-walked once per small stream, so the guard must be per chain. T7 is the same sector-chain primitive in a second, publicly exposed implementation with the cleanest dismissal of all (no Reader calls Shared\OLE), which is exactly the absent-plus-dismiss shape DeepSeek misses. T9 is a second decompression implementation (ZipArchive instead of zlib gzip) in the same CWE-409 family, dismissed as a different container primitive. This beats a gzip-only design (one easy judgement), and it beats adding T2/T8: those sit in the two files the fix already touches and their 'correct' behaviour is contestable (no amplification; bounded loops), so tests around them would be arguable rather than discriminating, and they add no new dismissal reason.
